headline: Govt employees may get 5-day Durga Puja break if Oct 22 declared holiday
summary: The government is considering declaring October 22 a public holiday, which would create a continuous five-day holiday for government employees.
details: Government employees could enjoy a five-day break during Durga Puja this year if the cabinet approves a proposal to declare October 22 a public holiday.

caption:
A 5-day holiday for Durga Puja? The government is considering a proposal to extend the break for government employees.

Government employees could enjoy a five-day break during Durga Puja this year if the cabinet approves a proposal to declare October 22 a public holiday.

Under the existing schedule, October 20 is a holiday for Nabami and October 21 is a public holiday for Dashami.

Government offices are currently scheduled to remain open on Thursday, October 22, followed by the regular weekend on Friday and Saturday, October 23 and 24.

A proposal to declare October 22 a holiday by executive order is being prepared for the next cabinet meeting.

An official from the Prime Minister's Office stated that a preliminary decision has been taken to declare the day a holiday.

If approved, government employees will be required to work on a subsequent Saturday to compensate for the October 22 holiday.

headline: 1,104 dead as measles outbreak toll passes 1,100 in Bangladesh
summary: Five more suspected measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours, with Dhaka Division recording the highest fatality rate.
details: According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the total number of deaths linked to the measles outbreak has reached 1,104. Five suspected deaths were reported in the last 24 hours alone.
The latest fatalities occurred in the Dhaka Division (three deaths), Sylhet Division (one death), and Chattogram Division (one death).
Dhaka Division has been the hardest hit, accounting for 451 deaths from suspected measles symptoms, followed by Sylhet with 177 and Rajshahi with 93.
In the last 24 hours, 1,255 people sought hospital care for measles symptoms, with 1,186 being admitted to hospitals across the country.
The DGHS has been tracking the outbreak since March 15, reporting a total of 190,510 suspected cases and 21,392 confirmed cases.
Hospital admissions have reached 168,655, while 161,798 patients have been discharged since the tracking began.
caption:
Over 1,100 people have died from a measles outbreak in Bangladesh, with 5 deaths reported in just one day.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the total number of deaths linked to the measles outbreak has reached 1,104. Five suspected deaths were reported in the last 24 hours alone.

The latest fatalities occurred in the Dhaka Division (three deaths), Sylhet Division (one death), and Chattogram Division (one death).

Dhaka Division has been the hardest hit, accounting for 451 deaths from suspected measles symptoms, followed by Sylhet with 177 and Rajshahi with 93.

In the last 24 hours, 1,255 people sought hospital care for measles symptoms, with 1,186 being admitted to hospitals across the country.

The DGHS has been tracking the outbreak since March 15, reporting a total of 190,510 suspected cases and 21,392 confirmed cases.

Hospital admissions have reached 168,655, while 161,798 patients have been discharged since the tracking began.
